title: rescale-fusion: fuse input/residual scaling into attention kernels for INT8/FP8 paths
author: Priya Shah
body:
Motivation: Quantized inference currently pays an extra memory and compute penalty when per-channel or per-tensor rescaling (dequant/recover scale factors used by SmoothQuant-like flows) is performed as a separate tensor broadcast + elementwise pass before the attention kernel. This PR introduces a lightweight "rescale-fusion" phase that folds input/residual scaling into attention microkernels to remove a stand-alone dequant/rescale tensor pass for common cases.

What changed (summary):
- Implemented fused-rescale variants of scaled-dot-product attention kernels for INT8 and FP8-backed execution paths. The kernels accept compact scale metadata and apply rescale when loading Q/K/V tiles to avoid allocating an intermediate dequantized tensor.
- Compiler/runtime: added a kernel vectorizer and small codegen pass that detects a pattern (dequant -> matmul-attn) and rewrites the callsite to the fused kernel when safe. Safety checks include: matching per-head scale shape, quantization bitwidth alignment, and KV-cache layout invariants.
- Scheduler: continuous-batching scheduler receives a hint to prefer fused-kernel-capable workers for mixed-precision flows; added a cheap runtime predicate so small batches still use fused kernels when applicable.
- KV cache: adjusted alignment and windowing metadata so fused-loads can stream KV shards without an extra reshuffle. The change is backward-compatible with existing cache layouts via a compatibility flag.
- SmoothQuant: moved an optional static calibration step into the model-compile stage (when provided) to emit per-channel scale metadata bundled with the model artifact; fallback produces runtime scale broadcasts that still work with the fused kernels but with reduced benefit.

Why this is safe: The fused kernels are instrumented with assertions verifying scale shapes at kernel entry and will fallback to the prior codepath if checks fail. We also keep a feature flag to gate production rollout per-customer. Unit and integration tests ensure numerically consistent outputs to within tolerance e-3 for int8 flows and e-4 for fp8 flows.

Benchmarks: (on c6-gpu-dedicated pools, seq_len=1024, batch=4)
- INT8-only path: throughput +12% on average, p95 latency -9%
- FP8-only path: throughput +8%, p95 latency -6%
- Mixed INT8/FP8 (smoothquant workload): throughput +18%, p95 latency -12%
Memory: peak working set reduced by ~22% due to removal of intermediate dequant tensors.

Rollout plan: canary on dedicated pools, enable feature flag for small subset of customers, track token-level loss/regression metrics using existing Optimize hooks. If regressions exceed thresholds, automatic fallback to old path occurs.

Migration notes: when a model is compiled with per-channel scale metadata available (recommended), the model manifest will contain a new "rescale_meta" field. Older runtimes ignore this field. Customers using Private deployments should update the private installer (small agent bump included here) to get the kernel library with fused variants.

Related tickets: ENG-7421 (kernel fusion design), ENG-8278 (smoothquant compile integration), SUP-410 (incident: high p95 during mixed-precision rollout).

Checklist: 
- [x] Kernel implementation and unit tests
- [x] Compiler/vectorizer pass and integration tests
- [x] Scheduler hints and e2e perf tests
- [x] KV cache alignment change + compatibility flag
- [x] Documentation (model manifest and rollout guide)

release_notes: Fused rescale-attention kernels for INT8/FP8 flows. Improves throughput ~8-18% depending on workload, reduces memory by ~22%. Requires model compilation to emit optional rescale_meta for max benefit; backward-compatible runtime fallback available.
